snippet:

Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. snippet:

snippet:

Abstract: Empirical finance research often reuses natural experiments to study other outcomes, raising concerns about multiple testing and publication bias. We use AI agents to run a multiverse analysis of 324 papers that reuse 13 natural experiments. Abstract: Every empirical analysis on observational data rests on dozens of defensible analytical choices ("forks") that its readers cannot see. snippet:

Abstract: Scientific discovery requires revisiting the hypotheses in light of new evidence and identifying promising directions beyond those already explored. snippet:

title: Pandora's Toolbox Or Why Agent Safety Cannot Be Verified
snippet:
arXiv:2611.25325v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Present artificial intelligence agents are constructed by means of a coupling between a fixed language model with a general computing device. We show that this coupling makes safety undecidable. In particular, we show that given some dangerous program, no algorithm can predict whether an agent will run such a program that is semantically equivalent. snippet:

Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can now autonomously conduct AI research by writing code and running experiments. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used not only to power AI agents but also to build them. snippet:

Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems replicate through deployment, vary through training, and compete for computational resources. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) support scientific research, but some of that assistance can also undermine research integrity.
